podcast.title: Grammy Win for "No Time to Die" Amidst Film Delays (2020)
podcast.body: Billie Eilish's theme song for "No Time to Die" was released in February 2020, intended to align with an early movie release date. However, the film suffered multiple postponements due to COVID-19, leaving the song without its accompanying film for 18 months. Despite this unusual circumstance, the song still managed to win a Grammy Award for Best Song, Written for Visual Media. "Meanwhile, though, it somehow managed to win a Grammy award for Best Song, Written for Visual Media."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bond...James Bond...Music

podcast.title: Youngest Bond Theme Performer (2020)
podcast.body: Billie Eilish holds the distinction of being the youngest person ever to record a James Bond theme. She was 18 years old when she co-wrote and recorded "No Time to Die" with her brother Finneas O'Connell in late 2019. "Billy Eilish was 18 at the time this song was written and recorded. And that makes her the youngest person ever missing a Bond theme."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Bond...James Bond...Music

podcast.title: Youngest Major Grammy Sweeper (2020)
podcast.body: In 2020, Billie Eilish was the youngest nominee in Album of the Year, Record of the Year, and Song of the Year, and she swept all of them. This sweep was described as "prescient" given her subsequent Oscar and multiple Grammy wins, marking her as a successful young talent. "In 2020, Billie Eilish was the youngest nominee in album of the year, record of the year, and song of the year. And she swept all of them."

podcast.body: Billie Eilish is cited as one of the "millennial or zoomer" artists who have placed ten or more songs on the Hot 100 simultaneously in the digital era, indicative of an imperial moment. "Billie Eilish to Olivia Rodrigo."

podcast.title: Animal Rights and Environmental Activism
podcast.body: Animal rights are a major focus for Billie Eilish, and she consistently promotes vegetarianism. She is also an environmental activist, actively participating in a social media campaign to protect the Great Barrier Reef in Australia. "Animal rights are a big thing with her. She promotes vegetarianism all the time. Billy is also an environmental activist getting involved in a social media campaign to protect the great barrier reef in Australia."

podcast.title: Biggest Tweetpop Descendant
podcast.body: Billie Eilish is identified as the most prominent and "biggest" artist whose music embodies the enduring influence of Tweetpop into the 21st century. Her widespread success showcases how the dreamy, introspective, sensitive, and vulnerable qualities of Bedroom Pop, a direct spin-off of Tweetpop, can achieve significant mainstream appeal. "And then there's the biggest of them all. Billy Eilish."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Color Performance - Early Career Impact
podcast.body: Billie Eilish performed on Color (another YouTube live channel known for its minimalist style) when she was just 15 years old and had only 15,000 subscribers on her channel. The impact of this performance was so significant that she repeated it the following year, and that second live performance has now reached nearly 200 million views. "La californía nactua allí cuando tenía apenas 15 años y solo 15 mis suscriptores en su canal."

podcast.title: Exceptional Digital Sales and Early Achievements
podcast.body: At a young age, Billie Eilish has achieved remarkable commercial success, with only 25 other artists having sold more digital songs than her. All of these accomplishments were realized before she turned 21. "Only 25 more people have sold more digital songs than her. And again, all this happened before the age of 21."

podcast.body: Billie Eilish now has her own signature ukulele, which is produced by Fender, a company renowned for its guitars. "Billy Eilish now has her own signature ukulele. It's made by Fender, the guitar people."

podcast.title: Grammy Awards Sweep
podcast.body: Billie Eilish became the youngest person ever to sweep the four major Grammy Awards: Best New Artist, Record of the Year, Song of the Year, and Album of the Year. As of now, she has won a total of seven Grammys, along with two American Music Awards, three Brit Awards, numerous MTV awards worldwide, and a Golden Globe. "She became the youngest person to sweep the big awards of the Grammys, best new artist, record of the year, song of the year, and album of the year. She's won seven Grammys in total as of now."

podcast.title: Grammy-Winning Home Recordings
podcast.body: Billie Eilish achieved immense success, including multiple Grammy wins, by transforming home recordings made with her brother into a landslide of critical and commercial acclaim, demonstrating the potential of bedroom pop. "But the biggest of them all was Billy Eilish, who turned some home recordings with their brother into a landslide of Grammy wins."

podcast.title: Impact on Fashion Industry
podcast.body: Her influence extends to the fashion world, notably leading to her appearance on the cover of *Vogue* and convincing Oscar de la Renta to cease using real fur in their designs. "Even Vogue put her on the cover and she got Oscar D. Laurenti to stop using real fur."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Influential Visual Image and Body Positivity Advocacy
podcast.body: Billie Eilish's visual image has been highly influential, as she consciously refuses to adhere to music industry expectations for women to dress provocatively. Her preference for baggy clothes is a deliberate response to counter judgment of women's bodies, and she has been very outspoken against body shaming, which has had a significant impact. "She refuses to play the music industry game where women are supposed to dress sexy. The baggy clothes are a calculated response to people judging women's bodies. She's been very outspoken about body shaming."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

podcast.title: Modern Legacy of Witchhouse
podcast.body: Billie Eilish is considered the clearest current example of the Witchhouse legacy. Her whispering sound, deep bass, and overall dark and melancholic aesthetic seem to combine and dethrone mainstream codes, reflecting what Witchhouse proposed a decade earlier. "Su sonido sus rantes, sus bajos profundos, y sobre todo su estética oscura y melancólica, parece la combinación del trono de los códigos del midstream, de todo lo que el witchhouse propuso una década antes."

podcast.title: Most Successful Bedroom Pop Artist
podcast.body: Billie Eilish is regarded as the most successful Dreampop/bedroom pop artist of the current century, reflecting the genre's continued impact and evolution.

podcast.title: Ongoing Tic Symptoms
podcast.body: Although many of Billy Eilish's Tourette Syndrome symptoms have subsided over the years, some persist, becoming noticeable if one spends enough time with her. These tics include wiggling her ear back and forth, clicking her jaw, raising her eyebrows, and flexing her arm, all involuntarily. Interestingly, these tics never seem to manifest when she is performing. "She'll wiggle her ear back and forth, click her jaw, raise her eyebrows, flex her arm, all involuntarily."

podcast.title: Openness About Mental Health and Tourette Syndrome
podcast.body: Billie Eilish is candid about her mental health issues, including depression, which she has suffered from for years. She is also open about her Tourette syndrome, encouraging other sufferers to speak about it to help reduce the associated stigma. "And she's very open about mental health issues, including depression, something that's doctor for years. And she's open about her Tourette syndrome, urging other sufferers to talk about it and reduce the stigma."

podcast.title: Oscar Win and Continued Success
podcast.body: Four years after her 2020 Grammy sweep, Billie Eilish continued to accumulate awards, including an Oscar win, multiple Grammy wins, and was poised to dominate another award season, solidifying her status as a successful young artist. "as Eilish comes off an Oscar win, multiple Grammy wins, and is poised to dominate another award season, that 2020 sweep looks prescient."

podcast.title: Public Discussions of Tourette
podcast.body: Billy Eilish has candidly spoken about her Tourette Syndrome on camera with both David Letterman and Ellen DeGeneres, though she doesn't discuss it often. She describes the condition as exhausting but a part of her life, and she is willing to talk about it if it helps others facing similar challenges. "Billy doesn't talk about her Tourette that often, but when she does, she's very candid."

podcast.body: Billie Eilish is among the artists who have supported Record Store Day, an annual celebration of vinyl and independent record stores. "to Billy Eilish."

podcast.title: Tourette Syndrome Diagnosis
podcast.body: Billy Eilish has been very open about living with Tourette Syndrome, a neurological condition that causes involuntary tics or movements. Her symptoms began at a very young age, including blinking and rapid jaw clicks, making it seem like her teeth were chattering. She received a formal diagnosis when she was 11. "This is a neurological condition that results in involuntary ticks or movements."

xref.title: Broad Influence on Contemporary Artists
xref.body: Her distinctive style and sound have had a profound impact on a wide range of artists across different genres. Influences can be heard in the music of Florence Welch (Florence + The Machine), Lady Gaga, Lana Del Rey, Alessia Cara, and Billie Eilish. Male singers such as Bruno Mars and Sam Smith also credit Amy as an inspiration. "Her influence can be heard in the music of any number of artists. Florence Welch or Florence in the machine. Lady Gaga, Lana Del Rey, Alissa Carrier and Billie Eilish."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

xref.title: Diverse Fanbase
xref.body: Her fanbase is wide-ranging, including prominent figures like Billie Eilish, Ed Sheeran, Charlie XCX, Willow Smith, and Olivia Rodrigo. Even Rob Halford of the metal band Judas Priest openly expresses his admiration for Avril Lavigne. "Fans include Billy Eilish, Ed Sheeran, Charlie XCX, Willow Smith and Olivia Rodrigo, even Rob Hulford of Judas Priest says he's a fan of Avril Lavigne."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

xref.title: Ongoing Criticism and Immense Influence
xref.body: Despite her charitable work and evolving social views, Lana Del Rey remains subject to criticism, primarily regarding the themes and imagery present in her music. Nevertheless, her influence on contemporary artists such as Billie Eilish, Lorde, and Halsey is considered immense. "Even with all that, Lana is subject to all sorts of criticism, mostly over the themes and imagery in her music. At the same time, though, her influence has been immense. Could there have been a Billie Eilish or Lord or Halsey without Lana Del Rey? I'd say no."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women of the 21st Century

xref.title: Shirley Manson's Influence
xref.body: Shirley Manson, the Scottish singer drafted into the American band Garbage, has had a notable impact on contemporary artists. Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evanescence, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish, and Lana Del Rey. "Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evan Essence, Katie Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey."
